Levers, each needs a card: (1) key sets that store key HASHES plus a pointer-free comparison, so no String is stored twice; (2) readers that only match (is_nil, all_prim, all_obj, row.lock) with no escape anywhere downstream, so borrow inference can lend; (3) a packed string representation (U32 array chunks) for keys and values - a carrier change across text/json/encode/decode. NE-012 (BN.cmp) and NE-014 (trim_end) are the two measured edges of this problem.

title: Nested repeated-key merge is still quadratic: one key repeated n times whose object grows (4000: 2.7 s vs the original's 0.04 s)
description:
Follow-up to toon_bend-qgu, which fixed the OUTER chain (n distinct keys each repeated: 2.51 s ->
0.08 s at n=2000, linear again). The nested case is untouched: a document of n lines 'a:' each
carrying a distinct inner key makes the merge target object grow, and dup.merge still calls dups()
over that chain, so each occurrence costs O(i). Measured 2026-09-22 on the fix (8 cores): grow1000
0.15 s, grow2000 0.73 s, grow4000 2.72 s (before the fix: 0.16 / 0.74 / 2.45); the original does
4000 in 0.04 s. A fix needs the value tree itself to stay map-backed while an object is open (the km
of a merged child would have to persist across occurrences), which is a carrier change one level
deeper than qgu; EXP-004's precedent applies. diff-fuzz scale passes today because its 'every key
repeated' input is the outer shape, so add a lens input of the nested shape with the fix.

DESIGN NOTES (2026-09-22, from the qgu fix session; do not re-derive):
1. Why qgu's fix does not reach this: the frame's J.KM makes the OUTER object's lookup/update O(log), but a
   repeated key whose value is an object still merges through dups() over the STORED inner chain, which grows.
2. Three designs were considered.
   (a) HOT CHILD: the frame caches (key, inner chain reversed, inner KM) for the LAST merged key; consecutive
       repeats become O(1) amortised, a key switch flushes (O(i), today's cost, no regression). Fixes the lens
       input and the common shape; a repeat one level deeper is still quadratic. ~4 frame fields + flush logic.
   (b) MAP-BACKED VALUE TREE (general): the decoder builds objects as MV{chain, KM-of-MV} and materialises
       J.Json at close. Fixes every depth. Needs a KM whose values are MV (the current KM is monomorphic over
       Json), so ~40 lines of carrier plus every object-construction site in decode.bend.
   (c) DEFER the merge to the parent's close: rejected. The merge would stop happening in attach order, and the
       first 'Duplicate sibling key' failure is reported by document position; an inner object closes before the
       outer object's later keys attach, so two failures in different objects could swap. It would need the
       pending duplicates to carry their line numbers and G.dup to keep the smallest, which is more machinery
       than (b) for less generality.
3. Recommended: (b). Do it when port/decode.bend is not being edited by a review round, and re-run
   diff-fuzz scale (the nested inputs are committed in 0e4f1d0 and are RED until this is fixed).
